text:
Lina (CS): Heads-up — Acme Prod Ops opened an escalation: after our most recent canary they see Spanish and Korean answers suddenly including English phrases and irrelevant additions. Customer: "Responses were fine yesterday, after the deploy half our Spanish responses include English sentences and some hallucinated city names."

acme-prod-ops: Repro snippet from production traffic:
```
PROMPT (es): "Traduce al español: Where is the nearest train station?"
RESPONSE: "Translation: The nearest train station is downtown. La estación está a dos cuadras. Also check the @support hotline."

PROMPT (ko): "서울에서 가장 가까운 지하철역은 어디인가요?"
RESPONSE: "The nearest subway is Central Station. 지하철은 중앙역입니다. Please see https://acme.example/status for ETA."
```

Matt S.: Thanks Lina. Do we have request_ids / model name / region / approximate timestamps from the customer? Also, what was the canary percentage and model alias used in the rollout?

acme-prod-ops: Provided request IDs: rId=prod:48f2c9 (Spanish), rId=prod:48f2d1 (Korean). Model header they send: "model: r-infer-xlarge:2026-03-15". Canary started at 10% around 2026-03-15T14:05Z and ramped to 20% at ~14:20Z. We saw degradation starting ~14:10Z.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: rollout r-infer-xlarge:2026-03-15 -> alias r-infer-xlarge:latest at 2026-03-15T14:02Z. Canary policy: 10% for 15m then 20% for 30m. No automatic rollback triggered.

Sophia (Eng): Ok. Two quick hypotheses: 1) model variant mismatch (quantized fallback) with different tokenizer/locale behavior; 2) prompt preprocessing (Accept-Language or locale header) not being passed to the model variant during fallback.

Raj (Infra): I'm pulling routing logs for those request_ids now. Quick note from the layer: around the time window we had one autoscale event that moved ~18% of traffic to a GPU pool with the variant r-infer-xlarge-quant. Tokenizer checksum for that variant differs (sha256 mismatch) vs the main variant — suspicious.

Matt S.: Can we repro locally? acme-prod-ops, could you run this minimal curl (they run it and paste output):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"r-infer-xlarge:2026-03-15","input":"Traduce al español: Where is the nearest train station?","temperature":0.0}'
```

acme-prod-ops: Ran that exactly. Response matches the broken output above (English prefaced then Spanish). We also tried adding header `Accept-Language: es-ES` and got the same.

Sophia (Eng): Can you add `-H "X-Session-ID: trace-789"` and paste the full response headers? We want to see which backend variant handled the request (X-Backend-Variant / X-Model-Checksum).

acme-prod-ops: Response headers excerpt: `X-Backend-Variant: r-infer-xlarge-quant`, `X-Model-Checksum: ea7b9f2` (we have older checksum ea7b9f2c but earlier main was cb3d4aa).

Raj (Infra): That confirms fallback to quantized variant. That variant was intended for cost-savings but should be tokenization-compatible. Looks like tokenization mapping table got updated in the quantized build by accident — likely missing locale normalization for multi-byte punctuation.

Sophia (Eng): Repro steps for internal:
1) Use model alias `r-infer-xlarge:latest` with load routing to overcommit quantized pool.
2) Send Spanish prompt above at temperature 0.0.
3) Observe English prefix + mixed language output.

Sophia (Eng): Quick test patch idea: force tokenizer from main variant by setting header `X-Force-Tokenizer: main` in the routing layer. If that fixes it we can roll a targeted hotfix.

Raj (Infra): I can hotfix router to prefer main tokenizer for languages set in Accept-Language for the short term. Rolling that change to canary now (10% → 50% routing preference for main tokenizer when Accept-Language present).

deploy-bot: Routing change deployed to canary at 2026-03-15T15:10Z.

acme-prod-ops: After the routing tweak our quick run shows output back to expected Spanish-only translation. :relieved:

Lina (CS): Sharing this with the customer: thanks for the patience, we applied a routing patch that prefers the main tokenizer for requests with explicit locale headers. We'll follow up with a permanent patch tomorrow.

Sophia (Eng): Root cause summary for ticket: quantized build introduced an updated tokenizer mapping that mishandled certain locale punctuation/whitespace sequences causing the model to output its internal prefix in English before the localized text. Fix plan: 1) revert tokenizer diff in quantized build; 2) add CI compare-check (checksum compare between tokenizer artifacts) and Add unit tests for punctuation/locale sequences; 3) add routing safeguard to prefer main tokenizer until quantized build is validated.

Matt S.: Created CS ticket #CS-1092 and ENG tracking #ENG-3281. Assigning Raj and Sophia. Can we confirm whether any other customers hit this?

Raj (Infra): Quick scan of logs: ~4 clients showed similar symptoms (Asia+EU customers) during the 14:05–14:30Z window. I'll reach out to their CS owners.

Lina (CS): I informed the affected customers and offered rollback where necessary. Two customers accepted immediate rollback; Acme asked for the routing patch and is verifying in their integration today.

acme-prod-ops: Confirming — patched routing fixed our failing flows. We'll monitor for 24h and report back if we see any regressions. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Sophia (Eng): Pushing a reversion PR for the tokenizer diff now and will request a fast-track review.

Matt S.: Great triage. Closing the slacking loop — please update CS ticket with the routing change + PR links.

Lina (CS): Will do. Follow-ups: add postmortem if ENG-3281 ends up with any larger design changes.

Raj (Infra): Adding logs and request_ids to ENG-3281.

acme-prod-ops: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick response.

(reacts: :eyes: :100:)
